p.n: Almost no difference; 만일 sounds slightly more formal or written.

explain_en: 끓다 is for the liquid itself boiling: 물이 끓어요. When a person boils something, use 끓이다: 물을 끓여요.

dis.h: liquid bubbles by itself, no object

p.n: 끓이다 needs someone doing it, so the subject becomes a person.

examples.en: On weekends I grill meat on the grill in the yard.

examples.ko: 바람이 불어서 그릴에 불을 붙이기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's windy, so it's hard to light the grill.
This grill is easy to clean, so I like it.
I borrowed a big grill at the campsite.

examples.ko: 그릴 위에서 소시지가 맛있게 익고 있어요.
examples.en: Sausages are cooking nicely on the grill.
The grill is hot, so don't touch it.

explain: 캠핑이나 마당에서 고기를 굽는 기구는 '그릴'이라고 하고, 식당의 불판은 '불판', 생선을 굽는 철망은 '석쇠'라고 해요. 동사는 '굽다'를 써서 '고기를 굽다'라고 말해요. 같은 도구를 '바비큐 그릴'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: We grilled meat on a barbecue grill at the campsite.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그릴'과 같은 도구를 더 분명하게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A clearer name for the same cooking tool.

phrases.en: We grilled sausages on the grill and ate them.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses (으)로 to say which tool is used for cooking.

phrases.nuance_ko: 고기를 굽기 전에 불을 켤 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when lighting the fire before grilling.

explain_en: Grill appliance for cooking meat — outdoor camping or oven part. The device for grilling meat while camping or in a yard is '그릴'; a restaurant's hot plate is '불판' and a wire rack for fish is '석쇠'. The verb is '굽다', as in '고기를 굽다'. The same tool is also called '바비큐 그릴'.

t90.ax: The grill is hot, so don't touch it.
